newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada says news of mission caused refugee return.
newsitem.headline: Canada says news of mission caused refugee return.

text.p: Canada, claiming partial credit on Friday for the return to Rwanda of refugees, said it would be wrong now to cut the size of the planned international rescue mission to Central Africa.

"The initiative that was taken this week, beginning last weekend with the (Canadian) prime minister (Jean Chretien), is already I think beginning to pay its own dividends in terms of having a breakthrough," Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said.
Axworthy told a news conference that the imminent arrival of the mission had created the conditions for the return, one of the ultimate goals for ending the refugee problem.
"The fact that the force can now be there to further enhance and support that movement really allows us to tackle something that many people only a few days ago thought was intractable," he said.
He said that while the mission might now place more emphasis on resettlement of refugees in Rwanda, a very strong show of presence was still needed in the area.

"I don't think you want to dilute your efforts in any way now," the minister said, adding that airports in eastern Zaire needed to be secured and safe corridors provided for the hundreds of thousands of refugees remaining.
